name: settings-rail-chrome-and-focus-ring
description:
One defect showing in two states. Every rail item drew as a raised native button (no appearance: none), and no control in settings.css had a :focus-visible rule, so keyboard focus fell back to the browser's own ring. Both are fixed in the same settings.css pass: .settings-rail-item now resets appearance/background/border like every other button family here, and every interactive control takes its focus ring from overlay.css's convention (outline: 2px solid var(--ov-accent); outline-offset: 2px, or -2px on the segmented option whose sliding thumb sits too close for an outward ring).

Three captures, one launch: 'rest' right after open, 'selection' after an eval-driven click moves the selection with the mouse, and 'focus' after the rail's own ArrowDown handler moves it with the keyboard.

A first version of this scenario borrowed the Tab/Shift-Tab sequence from settings-tab-row-keyboard-focus-ring.json and got 'BUTTON, not a rail item' back from both its 'rest' and 'focus' evals - that scenario predates the open-time focus call, which installSettings() now runs at the end of open: root.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="selected"]').focus() (settings.js), so the rail already holds DOM focus before any key is pressed, and plain Tab immediately walks OFF it onto whatever plain-tabbable control follows (the roving tabindex leaves every other rail item at tabIndex -1, un-Tab-reachable). Measured instead of assumed this time, and one more assumption fell: both 'rest' (the open-time .focus()) and 'selection' (an eval-driven .click()) came back :focus-visible TRUE, not false. Neither is a real mouse press on the element - Chromium only suppresses :focus-visible on a button when focus arrives FROM an actual pointer press on that element, and a script call to .focus() or .click() carries no such press, so the browser treats both the same as a keyboard arrival. The rule ('selected without relying on a focus ring') therefore has to hold up with the ring ON, not just in the rarer case of a real mouse click - which is exactly why .selected keeps its own background-plus-accent-colour treatment rather than leaning on the ring's absence. PANES order (settings.js) is general, appearance, spaces, ... - the mouse click in 'selection' lands on appearance, so the ArrowDown in 'focus' steps from there to spaces, and railKey() (settings.js) answers ArrowDown/ArrowRight/ArrowUp/ArrowLeft only when the event's target is itself a '.settings-rail-item', calling selectPane(id, {keepFocus: true}) to re-focus the newly selected item synchronously inside the keydown handler.

Assertions read DOM state through cdp-eval rather than a pixel region: the rail was rewritten from the 220px top bar the older settings-rail-keys.json and settings-tab-row-keyboard-focus-ring.json scenarios measured into a 190px left column, so those scenarios' pixel regions are stale for this layout and reusing them would sample empty space. settings-cmd-comma.json already made this same call for the same reason.

actions.note: let the browser window finish first paint
Atrium MUST be frontmost or cmd+comma opens Finder Settings instead - observed in settings-tab-row-keyboard-focus-ring.json
open Settings; its menu item is not reachable from a scenario
window opens on General - the open-time .focus() already put DOM focus on the General rail item
Evidence: the rail at rest, only General selected - the resting/selected chrome must come from settings.css alone
General is the default pane, confirming the capture is really at the window's opening state

The open-time .focus() carries no mouse press, so Chromium treats it as a keyboard-equivalent arrival and the ring is expected ON here too - the selection has to hold up with it showing, not by hiding it

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="appearance"]'); if (!b) return 'no-pane'; b.click(); return document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="appearance"].selected') ? 'selected' : 'not-selected'; })()
actions.note: same element-targeted click settings-cmd-comma.json uses for this exact rail
Evidence: Appearance reads as selected (--ov-sel + accent) with General back at rest - the ring is expected to be riding along with this eval-driven click too, since it carries no real mouse press
The selected pane must stay legible as selected even with the ring on, since only a real mouse press (not this eval's .click()) would suppress it

THE MEASUREMENT. railKey() only answers when the keydown target is a rail item, which the click above already focused - one step moves appearance -> spaces (PANES order in settings.js) and re-focuses it via selectPane's keepFocus
renderSettings() is a synchronous DOM rebuild, no CSS transition on the rail - slack for the ssh/capture round trip, not an animation, same margin settings-rail-keys.json uses
Evidence: Spaces holds real keyboard focus - the ring must be the overlay's, not the browser default
confirms activeElement IS the selected rail item, not something else - drive the focus explicitly and prove it landed where the capture claims
a keydown-driven selectPane() re-focus is keyboard-modality, so the browser itself must agree this is a visible arrival

assertions.note: the browser window AND the settings window

assertions.desc: Cmd+Q still quits with the settings window open
